## Summary

B0–B7 are extra address registers, restricted to long data and AMMX addressing.

## Details

- Registers B are handicapped versus its brother A
- Bn is restricted to manipulate long data or ammx data
- The integer unit supports:
- movea.l &lt;ea&gt;,Bn &lt;ea&gt; does not allow An (or Bn)
- move.l Bn,&lt;ea&gt; &lt;ea&gt; does not allow An (or Bn)
- lea &lt;ea&gt;,Bn
- lea (Bn),An = move.l Bn,An
- addq.l #n,Bn
- subq.l #n,Bn
- cmp.l Bn,Dn
- &lt;ea&gt; supports E but not B using the bank prefix
- B can not be moved to another B
- B can not be exchanged.
- In the future the BANK prefix will support banked address modes.

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- B registers do not exist on the 68000–68060.

## Do / Don't

- DON'T move or exchange a B register with another B register.
- DON'T use An or Bn as `<ea>` in `MOVEA.L <ea>,Bn` or `MOVE.L Bn,<ea>`.
